texts.preamble: Himanshu G Moliya vs Adjudicating Officer on 6 August, 2025 C/Fa/66/2020 Judgment In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/First Appeal No. 66 of 2020 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr. Justice Devan M. Desai ================================================================ Approved for Reporting Yes ================================================================ Himanshu G Moliya Versus Adjudicating Officer & Ors. ============================ = = = ============================== = = = Appearance: Mr Jaydev Bhatt for Mr Hriday Buch(2372) for the Appellant(s) No. Mr Rahul Dave, Agp for the Defendant(s) No. 1 Rule Served for the Defendant(s) No. 2,3,4,5,6 ================================================================ Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Devan M. Desai Date : 06/08/2025 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are as under:- 3.1. On 04.03.2016, appellant visited the place of opponent Nos.2 to 6 with a Panch witness. In presence of opponent No.2, appellant found 15 kg packed tin of Groundnut oil of Gayatri Brand and about 10 tins were stored for retail sale. The samples which were received by appellant, were sent to Food Safety Officer in sealed cover. On 21.03.2016, the report of the Food Analyst found that the sample of Gayatri Singtel manufacturing month February 2016, B.No.4 is misbranded under Regulation No.2.2.1.2 of Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined Labelling) Regulations, 2011 and the provisions of the said Act, and Rules made thereunder in respect of the name of food in Gujarati language only. The manufacturers accepted order of the Adjudicating Officer and paid the penalty imposed upon them. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned order, the appellant has preferred this Appeal. Learned Appellate Tribunal has wrongly applied provisions of Section 80 (B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned advocate for the appellant, at the outset, submitted that the order impugned is bad in law and exoneration of opponent Nos.2 to 6 is nothing but an overlooking of the provisions of Section 26 (2) (ii) and Section 27 (2) (c) of the said Act. It is contended that learned Appellate Tribunal has committed an error by resorting to Section 80(B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act. It is further contended that no defence is available to respondent Nos.2 to 6 herein in the cases where an offence pertaining to the sale of any unsafe or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the food business operator was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of the food sold by him or that the purchaser having purchased any article for analysis was not prejudiced by the sale. It is further contended that before the Adjudicating Authority, the defence of due diligence was never raised and the statement dated 22.02.2017 was given by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/66/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined opponents stating that sample has been declared as misbranded and opponents will be careful in future with regard to compliance of provisions of the said Act and Regulations made thereunder. When the defence of due diligence was not raised before the Himanshu G Moliya vs Adjudicating Officer on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45226363/ 2 Adjudicating Authority, such defence of due diligence is not available to respondent Nos.2 to 6 before the learned Appellate Tribunal. 5. Per contra, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 has contended that learned Appellant Tribunal has rightly applied the provisions of Section 80 (B) (2) (d) (i) of the said Act and acquitted respondent Nos.2 to 6, and rightly [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order of penalty. It is further contended that the reliance placed upon by the appellant on Sub- section (E) (iv) of Section 80 is not applicable.
